item.title: Add and Configure Components
item.description:
A component is one piece of infrastructure in a design, and its configuration is what Kanvas applies when you deploy. This guide covers placing components on the canvas, editing their configuration, and moving them around by duplicating, copying, and pasting.

You need a design open in Designer mode. Designer is the only mode that allows authoring.

Add a component 🔗

Kanvas offers several ways to place a component. All of them produce the same result: a component in the design, with its configurator open beside it.

item.title: Create Relationships
item.description:
Relationships record how components connect, and Kanvas keeps related configuration in sync once they exist. You create some relationships by hand and Kanvas creates others when it evaluates the design. This guide shows which is which, how to create each kind, and how to remove or hide them.

Relationships work only in Designer mode. For what each kind means, read Relationships.

Kind You create it by You remove it by
Edge (network, mount, reference, and other edge subtypes) Picking an edge from a component’s handle and dragging to a target Selecting the edge and choosing Delete
Hierarchical, inventory Dropping a component onto a compatible parent Dragging it out, or choosing Move Out of Parent
Hierarchical, wallet Dropping a component onto a compatible host Deleting the component, or choosing Move Out of Parent
Hierarchical, alias Kanvas creates it during evaluation Deleting the alias component
TagSets (shared labels) Giving components matching labels Changing the labels so they stop matching
Annotation edge Drawing with the Pen tool Selecting the edge and choosing Delete

Create an edge relationship 🔗

Edge relationships connect components that exchange traffic or depend on one another, such as a Service and a Deployment.

item.title: Whiteboard on the Canvas
item.description:
Whiteboarding in Kanvas (3:41) follows one late-night incident from page to postmortem on a single live design. Its page has chapters and a transcript.

Whiteboarding lets you diagram freely on the same canvas as your infrastructure. You draw shapes, text, freehand strokes, and lines to explain intent, and they sit beside real components in one design. It is on by default and available on every plan.

item.title: Pin Models to the Dock
item.description:
Pinning a model puts its icon in the dock at the bottom of the canvas, so you can reach its components without opening the full palette. Pins belong to your account. They are not stored per design or in the browser, so they follow you across designs, browsers, and devices.

Pinning works in Designer mode. In Operator mode the dock does not show pinned models.

Pin a model 🔗

Hover a model row in the component palette and use the pin icon. Its tooltip reads “Pin To Dock”. The shape palette offers the same pin on each shape category row.

item.title: Work with Tags
item.description:
Tags are the key-value labels and annotations on a component. When components share matching labels, Kanvas groups them in a TagSet, a shaded region drawn around the matching components. Use tags to see which components belong together, such as the Service and Deployment of one application.
